justification: canibuildit.com.au (and www) were 308-permanent-redirected to plotdetect.com.au by a next.config.js 'Legacy domains' block, so the domain showed nothing of its own — the public info site was only reachable at plotdetect.com.au. Removing the two canibuildit redirect rules so the domain serves the Next.js app (the public info site) directly. plotdetect.com.au is unchanged and continues to serve the info site. whatcanibuildhere.com.au redirect is left intact (not in scope).

break_it.scenario: canibuildit.com.au is not actually attached to the Vercel project, so removing the redirect leaves it serving nothing
break_it.what_happens: the domain could show a Vercel default/404 instead of the site
break_it.repro: hit canibuildit.com.au after deploy with the domain detached
break_it.how: the pre-existing redirect was served WITH an X-Vercel-Id for that host, which proves the domain is attached to the project and Vercel is routing it; removing the redirect makes that same routing serve the app

break_it.scenario: Two domains serving identical content dilutes SEO (duplicate content)
break_it.what_happens: search engines may split ranking between canibuildit and plotdetect
break_it.repro: both domains index the same pages
break_it.how: out of scope for this change and a deliberate product call to revive the domain; a rel=canonical to plotdetect can be added later if SEO consolidation is wanted. Functionally the site renders correctly on both

post_merge.secrets: None - no secrets or env vars.
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the Next.js frontend auto-deploys on Vercel from GitHub on merge; the redirect change takes effect on that deploy.
post_merge.manual_verify: After deploy, curl -sI https://canibuildit.com.au should return 200 (the site) instead of 308 to plotdetect.com.au; plotdetect.com.au still returns the info site homepage. whatcanibuildhere.com.au should still 308 to plotdetect.
